summary:
**NOTES (two books; keep separate)**

## BOOK 1: ELSIE'S WIDOWHOOD (Martha Finley, 1880; sequel to Elsie's Children)

**Preface:** author says public demanded a widowhood book; aim is showing Christ's love comforts bereavement.

**Cast:** Elsie Travilla (née Dinsmore, heroine; widow); Edward "Ned" Travilla (husband, d. Sept; "Edward", "papa"); father Horace Dinsmore (Mr. D, "papa", Oaks/Ion); Rose Dinsmore Travilla (Grandma Rose, Mr. D's wife; Edward's mother was Mrs. Travilla); Grandpa Travilla (Edward's father, lives at Ion). Children: Elsie (eldest daughter, engaged), Edward Jr. ("Ed", 17, to college), Violet ("Vi", daughter, "cricket" nickname from grandpa), Herbert, Harold, Rosie (little Rose), Walter (4, youngest). Lily = dead daughter (Elsie's first child) buried beside father. Lester Leland (sculptor, Elsie's fiancé, to Italy). Molly Percival (cripple, writer/translator, cousin; fall long ago), Enna Johnson (her mother, feeble-minded), Dick Johnson (Molly's half-brother, doctor), Bob & Betty Johnson (half siblings). Aunt Chloe (old mammy/nurse). Dr. Arthur Conly (cousin, doctor). Roselands: Mrs. Conly (Aunt Louise/Mrs. Conly, Mr D's sister? no—Mr. Dinsmore's aunt-line; Mrs. Conly = Louise), grandfather Dinsmore (Roselands; "Grandpa Dinsmore" elderly), sons Calhoun, Arthur, Walter (Lt, U.S. Army); daughters Isadore "Isa", Virginia. Oaks: Horace Dinsmore Sr., Horace Jr. Pinegrove: Howards. Ashlands: Carringtons, Herbert ("Herbie"?—no; Herbert Dinsmore is Elsie's brother's name in Ashlands line—treat as minor). Rose Lacey (Mrs. Lacey of Laurels). Cyril Keith (Pleasant Plains, Indiana; young minister; son of Cyril). Donald Keith (Cyril's brother, army lieutenant). Mary Keith (Donald's cousin, Uncle Donald's daughter). Mr. Embury (Magnolia Hall; widower of Mary; children Louis, Fred, Corinna, Madie). Mr. Jones (preacher denying devils). Mr. Mason (former pastor). Uncle Ben (old church member). Miriam Pettit. Mrs. Perkins, Susie, Fred Perkins. Charlie Perrine (Edward's college chum). Will Tallis (yacht Curlew owner). Amy Fletcher (invalid, Charlie's love), Ella Neff (teacher). Mr. & Mrs. Moses (Mrs. Moses cruel; Mr. Moses crippled). Mr. Ford (widower; courting Elsie later). George Boyd (villain who tried to kill Travilla; aunt Mrs. Carrington; maimed hand; scarred by Aunt Dicey's scalding shower).

**Plot in order:**
1. Vi finds Elsie crying with mamma; Lester Leland to Italy (1-3 yrs). Edward: "grace groweth best in winter." Molly despairs of love.
2. Engagement announced; dinner at Ion; relatives attend. Mrs. Conly, Virginia snub Fairview Lelands. Lester leaves; Elsie mourns.
3. September: Edward taken ill (sudden pain); Dr. Arthur, Dr. Barton, city consultants; no cure. Edward tells Mr. D "Is it so, Dinsmore?"; blesses children; dies. Last words to Elsie: "Precious little wife, eternity is ours!" Buried by Lily. Aunt Chloe: "He's mos' dar."
4. Elsie collapses; father takes her to rest; Scripture comfort ("When thou passest through the waters").
5. Children grieve; Rose consoles; Edward to take father's place; Mr. D as father. Elsie's first meal back.
6. Ion life; Edward to college; Harold & Herbert to be prepped by Mr. D; Edward's talk with mother on Bible, skeptics; Ed's allowance.
7. Nov: Arthur urges Mr. D to Viamede (warm climate). Elsie agrees; Molly, Enna, Isa invited; Dinsmores and Walter (Rosie, Walter) go.
8. New Orleans: Mr. D meets Boyd, begging; feeds him; offers help; Boyd moved to Viamede wing, aunt Mrs. Carrington invited. Elsie consents to his presence.
9. Viamede: Elsie's charity; Lester's letters; Herbert's Latin punishment (no food till recitation); Mrs. Travilla's lesson on perseverance; Harold asks mamma to plead.
10. Church at Viamede; Mr. Jones' false teachings (one devil); family Bible study on Satan, devils, chains, darkness; angels' protection.
11. Boyd dying in despair ("the door is shut"); Elsie forgives; he dies crying "God be merciful to me a sinner!" Mrs. Carrington's grief. Mamma tells children the lesson of Boyd's death.
12. Miss Miriam Pettit's prayer-meeting; Uncle Ben asks about Jones; Mrs. Travilla's view; Mr. Embury (Magnolia Hall, widower two years since Mary died; boys + 2 little girls) invited to Bible study; Elsie's suspicion.
13. Rev. Cyril Keith preaches "They hated me without a cause"; cousin of Dinsmores; Cyril stays; falls for Isa; Mr. Embury courts Molly.
14. Molly loves Embury; Elsie warns; Enna wants match; Molly's cripple-hunger; Molly's conversion doubts resolved.
15. Embury proposes to Molly (Corinna and Madie: "Yes, papa, I do!"); Mr. D approves.
16. Embury takes Molly to Magnolia Hall; engaged; Dick to settle at Viamede; wedding at Viamede (Mr. Keith officiates); Elsie gives $10,000; Embury $50,000 & jewels. Isa & Cyril engaged.
17. Conly reaction; Mrs. Conly's $25,000 dower promise on marriage; Cyril's cottage repaired. Isa's wedding June; Edward's sea-shore plans.
18. Edward home from college; cottage near Long Branch; Donald Keith visits; career talks (Harold→medicine, Edward→farming/agricultural college).
19. Mrs. Conly and Virginia arrive; Edward and Charlie Perrine; Mary Keith invites Violet to Colorado House (Ocean Beach); Violet sings "O Jesus, Friend unfailing" to Mr. Moses.
20. Mrs. Moses cruel; Amy Fletcher; Mary's plan for cottage.
21. Vi nearly goes home; Mr. D permits stay; Mary's cottage; Edward & Violet; Vi & Ella & Amy.
22. Cottage household: duties, daily worship, Shark River boating; Amy's health improves.
23. Sunday worship; Vi's disastrous dinner; Edward's hamper; trip to life-saving station; crossing inlet.
24. Will Tallis's yacht Curlew; Edward goes against Vi's plea; storm; wreck near Ocean Beach; life-car rescue; no lives lost.
25. Newspaper list; Mrs. Conly/Virginia gossip that Mr. Ford courts Elsie; Vi overhears; Elsie's reply: "Your beloved father is no more dead to me..." THE END. (Book ends with list of Elsie series titles.)

## BOOK 2: BINDLE (Herbert Jenkins, 1916)

**Foreword:** Blackwood's, Jenkins' reasons for writing.

**Cast:** Joseph "J.B." Bindle (bald, red nose, cricket cap blue-white, furniture-remover, beer and "little jokes", witty; Fenton Street, Fulham); Mrs. Lizzie Bindle ("Fairy", "Gospel Bells", Alton Road Chapel, sharp-tongued, asks "Got a job?"; cleanliness and religion); Ginger (gloomy, freckles, Chiswick, later enlists); Alfred Hearty (brother-in-law, greengrocer, 530 Fulham High Street; "Pull for the Shore, Sailors"; teeth, moustache); Martha Hearty (Mrs. Hearty, Mrs. B's sister, fat, wheezy, laughs); Millie Hearty (18, daughter; Charlie Dixon, shipping office, sweetheart; "Uncle Joe"); Smith (Hearty's assistant); Sanders (foreman at hotel; ex-foreman Brooks in later chapter); Wilkes (cough), Huggles, Ruddy Bill, Tom Cave, Weary, Ted, Whiskers. Professor Sylvanus Conti (Willie Wilkins; hypnotist; 13 Audrey Mansions, Queen's Club, West Kensington); rival John Gibson "English Mesmerist". Dick Little (doctor's son; wife Ettie; flat Beaufort Mansions/Chelsea), Tom Little (brother, St. Joseph's Oxford), Reginald "Gravy" Graves (St. Joseph's), Travers, Guggers (Guggers), Horace Trent (kangaroo costume). Lady Knob-Kerrick (Barton Bridge; daughter Ethel), Miss Isabel Strint, Thomas footman, Wilton butler, Mr. Cutts (Pack Horse landlord, red cap), Mr. Marsh, Mr. Greenhales (Roger), Sir Charles Custance (magistrate, Little Compton), Sergeant Wrannock, John Gandy (Dove and Easel, Little Compton), Mr. Richard Miller (Holmleigh; arms collection), Mr. Railton-Rogers (Branksome Road, 131 vs. 181), Mr. & Mrs. Granger (Lebanon Avenue, Chiswick). Rev. Mr. Sopley (Hearty's pastor), Rev. Edward Winch (missionary). Rev. Andrew McFie (Congregational, Scot), Rev. Mr. Slocum (vicar), Miss Slocum. Mr. Hearty's partner: Mrs. Gandy.

**Plot in order:**
1. Bindle & Ginger at Blue Boar; "marriage"/"tack" talk; Mrs. Bindle scolds "Lorst yer job?"; Bindle lied, pawns clock for 7s; plans stealing.
2. Finds Conti's keys; has duplicates cut; disguised in bandages; enters Conti's flat; Conti catches him, handcuffs, hypnotises, writes note to police; Bindle delivers note, gives up; returns Conti's property by post. Conti's brag to Evening Mail; Bindle's arrest; police court; Conti's fiasco ("Professor Conti's Great Hypnotic Fiasco").
3. Bindle's night walk; sausage stall.
4. Hearty home life; Sunday hymns; Bindle's "little jokes" (hymn-singing wrecking; missionary double-bed; grandfather clock weights). Millie asks to go to pictures with Bindle.
5. Bindle takes temp job as painter at Splendid Hotel (silent night work); foreman (Sanders) insults; Bindle gets to remove corridor door numbers; chambermaid's joke.
6. Hotel corridor chaos: room numbers swapped; guests half-dressed; clergyman mix-up; fireman restores order; Bindle's note-free escape. Sanders then visits Bindle home, Mrs. Bindle beats him with broom.
7. Bindle takes Millie to pictures; Charlie Dixon; Hearty collision; Charlie Dixon's "references" demand.
8. Harridge's Stores; Bindle to Barton Bridge Temperance Fete; Mr. Cutts; Dick Little's spiked lemonade; "English Rustic Fete"; Bindle's lemonade; Mr. Slocum & McFie drunk.
9. Fete riot; Lady Knob-Kerrick arrives; hose; McFie; police fight; Bindle ends in pantechnicon.
10. Mrs. Bindle: Hearty prayed for Bindle ("wheat-ear among thorns"). Bindle at Dick Little's flat; drinks; "Bindle the Incomparable".
11. Hearty's shop hoax: dog & housekeeper & nurse advertisement; crowds; Bindle clears; Bindle gives Hearty pineapple.
12. Dick Little & Tom with Reginald Graves (uncle Josiah Williams, Australian millionaire, hoax); Bindle as uncle. Oxford newspapers.
13. Oxford welcome; kangaroo horse; Bungem's supper; Bindle speech about Graves' grandfather; asparagus; Graves flees; Bushmen war-cry; Graves at St. Joseph's gate; Bindle returns to London.
14. Hearty's party; Mr. Sopley, Winch; "Blind Man's Buff", "Follow my Leader"; Bindle's vote of thanks reveals marriage history; Hearty "thankful".
15. Little Compton: Bindle & Ginger on Holmleigh job; Gandy; Sir Charles Custance's German invasion obsession; Wrannock; Gandy's bribed secrets; Greenhales; foreman Brooks; night arms episode; Wrannock, Greenhales, Gandy, Custance captured.
16. Amateur detectives: foreman captures four; police arrive; Miller; Bindle absent.
17. Bindle sacked from West London Furniture Depository; Branksome Road/Lebanon Avenue mix-up (Rogers vs. Granger); epilogue dismissal ("Lorst yer job?" "worth it").
18. Bindle tries enlisting (varicose veins), becomes special constable; Dick Little's elopement with Ethel Knob-Kerrick from Lady Knob-Kerrick's garden at Putney Hill; Guggers' Rolls-Royce; Bindle captured; Lady K's £5; Bindle released.
19. Friday Scarlet Horse coterie: Ruddy Bill, Ginger enlists; Bindle's views on war ("Gawd strike me dead" if not); Germany/Belgium; Whiskers; Tom Cave; Wilkes; Huggles.
20. Millie leaves home after Hearty forbids Charlie; Millie: "I wish he was my father"; Millie to Mrs. Bindle; Mrs. Bindle sobs; Bindle offers chapel.
21. Conclusion: Millie & Charlie engaged; Charlie enlisted; Hearty reconciled; Dick & Ettie Little; Bindle "funny things, women". 

Ends with list of other Jenkins titles.
